Water and bank routes near the Tilse and Nemunas shaped fishing, landing and carriage, affected by rising water. A party stopping there needed reliable water, fodder and someone able to negotiate with residents. River guards watched vessels, bank access and night landings. Escorts protected goods while allowing crews to rest, often needing local boatmen in unfamiliar water.

Water and bank routes near the Tilse and Nemunas shaped fishing, landing and carriage, affected by rising water. A party stopping there needed reliable water, fodder and someone able to negotiate with residents. Post income depended on continuing traffic; excessive demands encouraged detours. Garrisons and river works needed resources, while households' supply varied seasonally.
